**SEV2 — acknowledge within 15 minutes.**

Ingestion lag of 40 minutes for all customers matches the SEV2 definition: "a delay in data of more than 30 minutes." It's not SEV1 — that requires a customer-facing outage, data loss/corruption, a security breach, or a fault affecting more than 5% of the device fleet; a delay alone doesn't qualify.

SEV2 requirements beyond the 15-minute ack:
- Assign an incident commander (one person may also hold the communications role at SEV2).
- Open a channel named `#inc-YYYYMMDD-short-name`.
- First status page update within 30 minutes, then at least every 60 minutes even if nothing has changed.
- Mitigate first (roll back a recent deploy if suspected) before root-causing.

Two caveats: the first responder sets severity, and if in doubt you should pick the higher level — it can be lowered later. Also, if the lag is actually causing a full outage for any customer, or data is being lost rather than delayed, that would push it to SEV1 (5-minute ack, CTO notified, status page within 15 minutes).

Source: `oncall-incident-process`, section 6 (lines 50–59) and section 8.
